title: Fixed-count drought slopes were uncertain in two desert bird subsets in 1998-2022
abstract: We tested annual drought links to richness in a released subset of US desert bird records. Models used route and year effects, survey date and land cover. On surveys with at least 20 counted birds, fixed-count richness slopes were -0.033 and -0.342 species per unit lower SPEI-12 in 1998-2009 and 2010-2022. Both eight-test adjusted intervals included zero. Both paired raw-minus-fixed-count slope intervals also included zero. Drier surveys had lower estimated chances of reaching 20 birds. The released subset had fewer positive species than the supplied full-survey richness in all 729 surveys, so these data cannot test full-community rarefaction. Variable record coverage, selected counts, detection, few year clusters and shared routes limit inference. No causal drought or air pollution effect is established. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and independent count checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Annual drought slopes for released subset richness, fixed-count richness and their paired difference. All eight-test adjusted intervals shown cross zero.

citations.reason: Motivates the raw versus fixed-count measurement test; new data and new code.
